REQUEST
show two waves travelling in opposite directions, add them point by point to make a standing wave, and work out exactly where the nodes sit and why they never move

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two waves, going opposite ways
  2. At every point, add the two heights
  3. Some places never move at all

NAMES IN SCOPE
  A_C, B_C, K, OMEGA, SPAN, RIGHTWARD, LEFTWARD, title, t, ax_a, ax_b, ax_s, wa, wb, labs, SUM_C, ws, probe_x, m_a, m_b, m_s, readout, markers, NODE_C, DIM, ns, marks, rails, note, node_group

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  (none)

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 4 of 4, about 28 seconds
  intent: Where the nodes are, and why
  narration: Their positions are not a matter of looking carefully. Adding the two waves algebraically gives twice sine k x, times cosine omega t — and that splits cleanly into a part that depends only on position and a part that depends only on time. The wave is nailed down in space and free to breathe in time. It vanishes wherever sine k x is zero, which is every half wavelength, exactly.

```python
SUM_C = "#5CD0B3"
NODE_C = "#FC6255"
DIM = GREY_B
K = 2.0
half_lambda = math.pi / K
gaps = [round(b - a, 9) for a, b in zip(ns, ns[1:])]
assert len(set(gaps)) == 1 and abs(gaps[0] - half_lambda) < 1e-9
self.play(FadeOut(note), run_time=0.3)
ident = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"\sin(kx - \omega t) + \sin(kx + \omega t)",
                    font_size=26, color=DIM),
            MathTex(r"= 2\,\sin(kx)\,\cos(\omega t)", font_size=30, color=SUM_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.28, aligned_edge=LEFT)
ident.move_to(RIGHT * 4.3 + UP * 1.8)
self.play(Write(ident[0]), run_time=1.3)
self.play(FadeIn(ident[1], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=1.0)
split = VGroup(
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\sin(kx)", font_size=24, color=NODE_C),
                   Text("position only", font_size=17, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25),
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\cos(\omega t)", font_size=24, color=SUM_C),
                   Text("time only", font_size=17, color=DIM)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
split.next_to(ident, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(ident, LEFT)
self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for s in split],
                              lag_ratio=0.35, run_time=1.4))
spacing = VGroup(
            VGroup(Text("node spacing", font_size=18, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"{half_lambda:.3f}", font_size=24, color=NODE_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN),
            MathTex(r"= \tfrac{1}{2}\lambda", font_size=26, color=NODE_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=LEFT)
spacing.next_to(split, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(split, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(spacing, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=1.0)
self.play(t.animate.set_value(9.8), run_time=2.8, rate_func=linear)
self.wait(1.6)
```

REQUEST
show what a single neuron does — weights, a sum, a bias and an activation — and prove that without the activation two stacked layers collapse into one

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Three inputs, three weights

NAMES IN SCOPE
  IN_C, W_C, SUM_C, INPUTS, WEIGHTS, title, body, ys, first, note, in_dots, edges, in_labs, w_labs, src

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  (none)

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 2 of 4, about 20 seconds
  intent: Add them up, with a bias
  narration: Add the three contributions together, then add one more number that belongs to the neuron itself rather than to any input — the bias. It shifts the whole total up or down, which is what lets the neuron fire readily or reluctantly. Here the total comes to two point five three.

```python
W_C = BLUE_C
SUM_C = "#8B7FD4"
DIM = GREY_B
INPUTS = [0.9, -0.4, 0.7]
WEIGHTS = [1.2, -2.0, 0.5]
BIAS = 0.3
def weighted_sum(xs, ws, b):
    return sum(x * w for x, w in zip(xs, ws)) + b
z = weighted_sum(INPUTS, WEIGHTS, BIAS)
assert abs(z - 2.53) < 1e-9
self.play(FadeOut(note), run_time=0.3)
terms = VGroup(*[
            MathTex(rf"{x} \times {w} = {x*w:+.2f}", font_size=22, color=W_C)
            for x, w in zip(INPUTS, WEIGHTS)])
terms.add(MathTex(rf"\text{{bias}} = {BIAS:+.2f}", font_size=22, color=DIM))
terms.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=LEFT)
terms.move_to(RIGHT * 4.0 + UP * 1.7)
self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for t in terms],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2.0))
total = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"z", font_size=28, color=SUM_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {z:.2f}", font_size=30, color=SUM_C),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
total.next_to(terms, DOWN, buff=0.45).align_to(terms, LEFT)
self.play(Write(total), run_time=1.0)
self.play(Flash(body, color=SUM_C, line_length=0.18,
                        flash_radius=0.7, num_lines=12), run_time=0.9)
terms, total, z = terms, total, z

for i in range(m):
            # Skip 0 which never has an inverse
            if i == 0:
                gcd_val = m
                has_inverse = False
            else:
                gcd_val = math.gcd(i, m)
                has_inverse = (gcd_val == 1)
            
            # Find the inverse if it exists
            inverse = None
            if has_inverse:
                for j in range(1, m):
                    if (i * j) % m == 1:
                        inverse = j
                        break
            
            # Update the explanation
            if has_inverse:
                new_explanation = Text(
                    f"gcd({i}, {m}) = 1, {i} has inverse: {inverse}",
                    font_size=20, color=GREEN
                )
                circle_color = GREEN
            else:
                new_explanation = Text(
                    f"gcd({i}, {m}) = {gcd_val} ≠ 1, No inverse",
                    font_size=20, color=RED
                )
                circle_color = RED
            
            # Highlight the current circle

                number_circles[i][0].animate.set_stroke(YELLOW, width=3),
                FadeOut(explanation_text),

            self.play(

            )
self.wait(0.5)

divisors = VGroup()
for i, angle in enumerate([0, PI/2, PI, 3*PI/2]):

            # These weights represent the multiplicity of each point in the divisor

            divisor_group = VGroup(point, label, weight)
            divisors.add(divisor_group)
            self.play(Create(point), Write(label), Write(weight), run_time=0.7)
self.wait(1)
```
